subject: POC next steps — deployment mode qualification & owner rundown
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Carla Reyes <carla.reyes@parcela.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Today's call — deployment mode needs & next steps

Hi Carla — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned.

Call notes (short):
- Use cases: real-time parcel status generation + customer-facing summaries; ~120M tokens/month expected, peak short bursts at EOD.
- Compliance: SOC2 and ability to provide audit logs; prefer keys in KMS.
- Network: some services behind VPC with strict egress rules.
- Stakeholders you mentioned: Tom (CTO), Linda (SRE), procurement contact Laura.

Key decision: deployment mode. You flagged three options in the call: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput + isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict sysadmin controls. You said you're leaning toward a dedicated capacity model but wanted clarity on lead time and whether we can run an initial canary in hosted while Dedicated is stood up.

Proposed POC approach (high level):
1) Short sandbox (1–2 weeks) using Hosted API to validate prompts, success criteria, and eval suite (low friction).
2) Parallel Dedicated provisioning (2–4 weeks depending on capacity/region) with a canary cutover for production traffic.
3) If VPC constraints are non-negotiable, shift to Private plan and extend provisioning timeline (~4–6 weeks depending on network approvals).

Success criteria (please confirm):
- 95th percentile latency for customer-facing API < 250ms on typical requests
- End-to-end OKR: accuracy/regression against your prompt eval set (baseline TBD)
- No PII leakage and logs retention meeting your audit window
- Throughput: sustain 200 requests/minute for peak slices without degradation

Next steps I propose:
- Please confirm preferred POC mode (Hosted canary + Dedicated provision OR Dedicated-first OR Private).
- Share any network firewall/egress restrictions (I attached a quick network template).
- Confirm stakeholders and a target kickoff week (I put a proposed schedule below).

Attachments: redwood-poc-template.pdf (POC checklist), parcela-network-requirements.docx

I'll wait to hear which route you prefer and will loop in solutions (Mina) to draft a detailed POC plan and timeline.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com

From: Carla Reyes <carla.reyes@parcela.com>

Date: 2026-09-29T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Today's call — deployment mode needs & next steps

Thanks, Priyom — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: we are indeed leaning toward Dedicated capacity because our monthly volume looks steady and we need the isolation guarantees for SLA and auditing. Two caveats:

1) We need KMS integration for customer-managed keys (ideally bring-your-own-key).
2) Network egress: our environment blocks general outbound, so any Dedicated nodes must be reachable via a peered VPC or we need a clear egress list (IP ranges + FQDNs).

Stakeholders: Tom (CTO) — tom.nguyen@parcela.com; Linda Park (SRE) — linda.park@parcela.com; Procurement: laura.bennett@parcela.com.

Questions: what's the typical lead time to provision Dedicated in us-west? Can we start with Hosted as a canary while Dedicated is being prepared? Also, can you confirm whether Dedicated supports customer KMS today or is that on the roadmap?

If it helps, we're ok with a short Hosted canary to validate prompts, but procurement will want a timeline and an initial burn-rate estimate for a 3-month commit.

-Carla
VP Product, Parcela Logistics
carla.reyes@parcela.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap: Today's call — deployment mode needs & next steps (POC proposal)

Hi all — thanks, Priyom. Quick POC proposal below (we'll tailor after Laura confirms procurement constraints):

POC plan (6 weeks total, compressible):
- Week 0: Kickoff + creds + network clearance (we need Linda's SRE contact to open a short list of IPs/FQDNs or set up VPC peering).
- Week 1–2: Hosted canary (validate prompts, collect eval metrics, and harden prompt templates).
- Week 2–4: Provision Dedicated capacity (us-west); our standard lead time is ~10 business days for Dedicated in us-west once network + billing okayed — if priority, can expedite to ~5 business days with a bucket of reserved capacity.
- Week 4–6: Canary -> Dedicated cutover, load testing, SLO verification.

Success criteria (concrete):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 250ms for the canonical customer prompt set (we'll run K6 tests and measure p95).
- Quality: No degradation >2% vs your baseline for the eval prompts (we'll run automated evals).
- Reliability: No request error rate >0.5% during a 30-minute ramp test at peak load.
- Security: Key management — Dedicated supports Redwood-hosted keys today; customer-managed KMS for Dedicated is on our roadmap Q4-2026. As a workaround, we can encrypt request payloads in transit and ensure log redaction plus an audited key handshake.

Network options:
- Preferred: VPC peering in your cloud (we'll give exact peering steps).
- Alternative: static egress IP ranges + FQDN allowlist (see attached network doc).

Deliverables: POC runbook, success checklist, test scripts, and a one-pager cost estimate (Ben: see note below for pricing).

Attachments: redwood-poc-template.pdf, parcela-network-requirements.docx

I'll block time this week to onboard Linda/SRE and create the test harness once we get the green light.

— Mina
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

- Hosted canary consumption (estimated token burn for prompt tuning): $1.2k–$3k total depending on scope.
- Optional: priority provisioning / expedited bucket: +$8k one-time.

Ben will produce a formal quote + SOW once Laura confirms the procurement lead and any legal redlines. For now, please treat numbers as draft.

Ben Carter | Sales Eng, Redwood Inference
